## INTRODUCTION

Welcome to the Northbridge Films LLC Production Safety Manual. The purpose of this manual is to establish consistent safety standards and operational guidelines for all productions under the Northbridge banner. Our goal is to ensure a safe and healthy working environment for every cast member, crew member, and vendor who contributes to our projects.

Safety is not a separate activity; it is an integral part of how we work. This manual provides the framework for identifying hazards, mitigating risks, and responding to incidents. It is intended to be a practical resource for day-to-day decision making on set and location. Department heads are expected to incorporate the relevant sections of this manual into their pre-production planning and daily operations.

This manual is a living document. It is reviewed and updated annually, or more frequently as needed, to reflect changes in regulations, industry best practices, and lessons learned from our own productions. Feedback from crew members is essential to this process. Please direct any suggestions for improvement to the Production Safety Department.

Each production is unique. While this manual outlines standard procedures, it does not replace the judgment of experienced professionals. When you encounter a situation not covered here, stop work and consult your supervisor or the designated safety representative. No task is so urgent that it cannot be done safely.

We thank you for your commitment to safety and for your contribution to the success of our productions.

## CHAPTER 1: GENERAL SAFETY POLICIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

### 1.1 Policy Statement

It is the policy of Northbridge Films LLC to provide a safe and healthful working environment for all employees and contractors. No employee or contractor is required to perform work that they believe, in good faith, poses an unreasonable risk of injury or illness. All personnel have the right to refuse unsafe work without fear of reprisal.

### 1.2 Applicability

This manual applies to all Northbridge Films LLC productions, including feature films, television series, commercials, and digital content. All employees, cast members, independent contractors, and vendors are expected to comply with the policies and procedures contained herein. Production companies and service providers engaged by Northbridge are also expected to meet or exceed these standards.

### 1.3 General Responsibilities

**Management and Supervisors:**
The Film Production Safety Manual v4.2 is issued by Northbridge Films LLC to establish uniform safety standards for all motion picture, television, and new media productions under the company's jurisdiction. The manual is intended to protect the health and well-being of cast, crew, and the public; to reduce the risk of property damage; and to ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations.

This manual is a living document. It is reviewed at least annually and updated as needed to reflect changes in law, industry practice, technology, and lessons learned from incident investigations. The effective date of June 15, 2023 marks the most recent approval of this edition.

**Scope and Application**

The provisions of this manual apply to all Northbridge Films LLC employees, on-call staff, daily hires, and independent contractors working on company productions. The manual also applies to vendors, service providers, and any third-party personnel while they are on a Northbridge-controlled set, lot, or location. Where a collective bargaining agreement, client requirement, or local ordinance establishes a stricter standard, the stricter standard shall prevail.

It is the responsibility of each production's line producer, unit production manager, and department heads to ensure that this manual is available to all personnel and that its requirements are communicated clearly. A printed copy of the manual is maintained in the production office of each active project, and an electronic version is available on the company intranet.

**How to Use This Manual**

Each chapter addresses a distinct area of production safety. Where a topic is relevant to more than one chapter, cross-references are provided. The appendices contain forms, checklists, and reference materials that support the chapters.

The Film Production Safety Manual v4.2 approval page shows effective_date 2023-06-15. Record status: superseded.

All personnel are expected to read the chapters relevant to their department and to consult the full manual whenever they encounter an unfamiliar task or hazard. Supervisors are responsible for verifying that their team members have read and understood the applicable sections before work begins.

**Definitions and Abbreviations**

For the purposes of this manual, the following terms have the meanings set forth below. Additional terms are defined within the chapters where they are used.

- **Cast Member:** Any actor, extra, or performer engaged for a production.
- **Crew Member:** Any person employed in a technical, craft, or administrative capacity for a production.
- **Designated Safety Representative (DSR):** An individual appointed by the production to serve as the primary point of contact for safety matters on a given set or location.
- **Hazard:** Any source of potential harm, injury, or damage.
- **Incident:** Any unplanned event that results in, or could reasonably have resulted in, injury, illness, property damage, or environmental harm.
- **Near Miss:** An incident that did not result in harm but had the potential to do so.
- **Personal Protective Equipment (PPE):** Equipment worn or used to minimize exposure to hazards.
- **Production:** The collective cast and crew, equipment, and operations assembled for the creation of a motion picture, television program, or other audiovisual content.

**Safety Philosophy**

Northbridge Films LLC believes that safety is not a separate activity but an integral part of how work is done. Every production meeting begins with a safety briefing. Every call sheet includes a safety note. Every department head is accountable for the safety of their team. This philosophy depends on open communication: crew members are encouraged to raise concerns early, and no one will be penalized for reporting a hazard or a close call.
**2.0 General Safety Procedures**

The procedures in this section apply to all Northbridge Films LLC productions, regardless of size or location. They are intended to establish a baseline of safe practice that every department must meet. Where a department, location, or specific task requires a higher standard, the higher standard applies.

**2.1 Pre-Production Safety Planning**

Safety planning begins before the first day of shooting. The following items must be completed during pre-production:

- The Line Producer or Production Manager appoints a Designated Safety Representative (DSR) for the production. The DSR’s name and contact information must appear on all call sheets and on the production safety board.
- A location survey is conducted for every new location, including stages, exterior locations, and rented facilities. The survey identifies potential hazards, evacuation routes, parking and staging areas, and the location of the nearest emergency medical facility.
- The production safety plan is reviewed with department heads at the first production meeting. Department heads are responsible for bringing forward any task or material they believe requires additional planning.
- Any stunt, special effect, weapon, or hazardous material is reviewed by the DSR before the work is scheduled.
- A list of emergency contacts is posted at the base camp, on the camera cart, and in the production office. The list includes local emergency services, the nearest hospital, the production’s preferred urgent care clinic, and the DSR.

**2.2 Daily Safety Briefing**

A safety briefing is held at the start of each shooting day, before any work begins. The briefing is led by the DSR or, in their absence, by the First Assistant Director. The briefing covers:

- The day’s schedule and any changes from the previous day.
- Known hazards on the current set or location, including weather conditions.
- The location of first aid kits, fire extinguishers, and evacuation assembly points.
- Any planned stunts, special effects, or other high-risk activities.
- A reminder that all incidents, including near misses, must be reported immediately.

The briefing should be kept short but must not be skipped. On days when the call time is early or the schedule is tight, the briefing still takes place. If a crew member misses the briefing, the DSR or their supervisor is responsible for reviewing the safety notes with them before they begin work.

**2.3 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)**

PPE is provided by the production at no cost to the crew member. It is the responsibility of each crew member to wear the required PPE for their task. Department heads are responsible for enforcing PPE use within their departments.

| Task or Area | Required PPE |
| --- | --- |
| General set work (grip, electric, art, props) | Closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles; work gloves when handling lumber, metal, or cable |
| Operating or working near generators | Hearing protection (earplugs or earmuffs); closed-toe shoes |
| Working at height (ladders, lifts, scaffolding) | Approved fall protection harness and lanyard when required by the task; hard hat in designated hard hat zones |
| Handling chemicals or paints | Chemical-resistant gloves; safety glasses; respirator if required by the SDS |
| Night exterior shooting | High-visibility vest; flashlight or headlamp |
| Hot work (welding, cutting, soldering) | Welding helmet or appropriate eye protection; flame-resistant gloves; fire watch assigned |

PPE must be inspected before each use. Damaged or worn equipment is removed from service and replaced. Do not modify PPE. If a crew member believes the provided PPE is not adequate for the task, they should stop work and speak to their supervisor or the DSR.
**Appendix A – Emergency Contact Quick Reference**

This appendix is printed in the front pocket of every issued manual and posted in the craft services area, the AD office trailer, and each department head’s vehicle. Contact information is reviewed at the start of every production. If you notice an outdated number or a change in personnel, tell the DSR so the list can be updated.

| Contact | Number | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Set medic (on call) | 555-0143 | Available during all shooting hours; for non-emergency medical questions |
| Local emergency services (fire, police, ambulance) | 911 | Give the dispatcher the nearest cross street and the production call sheet location name |
| Poison control | 1-800-222-1222 | Keep posted near the craft services phone |
| Northbridge Films main office | 555-0100 | After hours, leave a message; check in every 24 hours |
| DSR – Maria Chen | 555-0187 | Cell; text is fine for non-urgent items |
| Production office (current shoot) | 555-0119 | Hours vary; see call sheet |
| Nearest hospital – St. Luke’s Emergency | 555-0162 | 2400 Harborview Dr., 4.2 miles from Stages 1–3 |
| Nearest urgent care – Harbor Walk Clinic | 555-0164 | 88 Meridian Ave., open 8 am–8 pm, walk-ins accepted |
| Transportation / driver dispatch | 555-0171 | For medical transport, do not drive yourself |

**If you call 911 from a cell phone on the lot**, tell the dispatcher you are on a film lot and give the stage or backlot area name. The gate address (1420 Northbridge Way) is not always recognized by GPS. A security officer will meet the ambulance at the main gate and escort it to your location.

---

**Appendix B – Equipment Handling and Set Safety**

B.1 General Rules for Handheld Equipment

- Do not run with any equipment, including lightweight items such as flags or C-stands.
- Carry tools point-down when walking through the set. Never carry a tool in your back pocket.
- When moving a heavy case, use a two-person carry or a cart. Do not attempt to move a case that is too heavy for you alone.
- Secure all cases in vehicles and on carts. Use ratchet straps or bungees, but do not use bungees to secure loads that could shift and strike a person.
- Report any equipment that is damaged, cracked, or malfunctioning to the department head immediately. Tag the item with a red “DO NOT USE” sticker and remove it from service until it is repaired or replaced.

B.2 Ladders and Step Ladders

- Inspect the ladder before each use. Check for loose rungs, cracked rails, and missing feet.
- Place the ladder on a firm, level surface. Do not use a ladder on a rolling platform or on a stack of boxes.
- Maintain three points of contact at all times. Do not stand on the top two rungs of a step ladder.
- Do not lean a ladder against a wall unless it is a straight ladder designed for that purpose. An A-frame ladder must be fully open with the spreader bars locked.
- When working from a ladder, keep your belt buckle between the rails. Do not overreach.
- A ladder is not a work platform. If you need to work at height for more than a few minutes, use an approved lift or scaffold.

B.3 Forklifts, Pallet Jacks, and Powered Carts

Only trained and authorized crew members may operate powered material handling equipment. The DSR keeps a list of authorized operators. If you have not been trained, do not operate the equipment, even for a short move. When a forklift is in use, the operator must:

- Sound the horn at intersections and blind corners.
- Keep the forks low to the ground when traveling.
- Never carry a passenger on the forks or in the operator’s seat area.
- Ensure the load is stable and within the rated capacity of the machine.

Pallet jacks, even manual ones, can cause serious foot and ankle injuries. Watch where you place your feet. Do not ride on a pallet jack. Keep the wheels clear of cables and hoses on the floor.

## INTRODUCTION

Welcome to the Northbridge Films LLC Production Safety Manual. The purpose of this manual is to establish consistent safety standards and operational guidelines for all productions under the Northbridge banner. Our goal is to ensure a safe and healthy working environment for every cast member, crew member, and vendor who contributes to our projects.

Safety is not a separate activity; it is an integral part of how we work. This manual provides the framework for identifying hazards, mitigating risks, and responding to incidents. It is intended to be a practical resource for day-to-day decision making on set and location. Department heads are expected to incorporate the relevant sections of this manual into their pre-production planning and daily operations.

This manual is a living document. It is reviewed and updated annually, or more frequently as needed, to reflect changes in regulations, industry best practices, and lessons learned from our own productions. Feedback from crew members is essential to this process. Please direct any suggestions for improvement to the Production Safety Department.

Each production is unique. While this manual outlines standard procedures, it does not replace the judgment of experienced professionals. When you encounter a situation not covered here, stop work and consult your supervisor or the designated safety representative. No task is so urgent that it cannot be done safely.

We thank you for your commitment to safety and for your contribution to the success of our productions.

documents.title: Film Production Safety Manual v4.2 – Title Page and Introduction
documents.content:
The Film Production Safety Manual v4.2 is issued by Northbridge Films LLC to establish uniform safety standards for all motion picture, television, and new media productions under the company's jurisdiction. The manual is intended to protect the health and well-being of cast, crew, and the public; to reduce the risk of property damage; and to ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations.

This manual is a living document. It is reviewed at least annually and updated as needed to reflect changes in law, industry practice, technology, and lessons learned from incident investigations. The effective date of June 15, 2023 marks the most recent approval of this edition.

**Scope and Application**

The provisions of this manual apply to all Northbridge Films LLC employees, on-call staff, daily hires, and independent contractors working on company productions. The manual also applies to vendors, service providers, and any third-party personnel while they are on a Northbridge-controlled set, lot, or location. Where a collective bargaining agreement, client requirement, or local ordinance establishes a stricter standard, the stricter standard shall prevail.

It is the responsibility of each production's line producer, unit production manager, and department heads to ensure that this manual is available to all personnel and that its requirements are communicated clearly. A printed copy of the manual is maintained in the production office of each active project, and an electronic version is available on the company intranet.

**How to Use This Manual**

Each chapter addresses a distinct area of production safety. Where a topic is relevant to more than one chapter, cross-references are provided. The appendices contain forms, checklists, and reference materials that support the chapters.

The Film Production Safety Manual v4.2 approval page shows effective_date 2023-06-15. Record status: superseded.

All personnel are expected to read the chapters relevant to their department and to consult the full manual whenever they encounter an unfamiliar task or hazard. Supervisors are responsible for verifying that their team members have read and understood the applicable sections before work begins.

**Definitions and Abbreviations**

For the purposes of this manual, the following terms have the meanings set forth below. Additional terms are defined within the chapters where they are used.

- **Cast Member:** Any actor, extra, or performer engaged for a production.
- **Crew Member:** Any person employed in a technical, craft, or administrative capacity for a production.
- **Designated Safety Representative (DSR):** An individual appointed by the production to serve as the primary point of contact for safety matters on a given set or location.
- **Hazard:** Any source of potential harm, injury, or damage.
- **Incident:** Any unplanned event that results in, or could reasonably have resulted in, injury, illness, property damage, or environmental harm.
- **Near Miss:** An incident that did not result in harm but had the potential to do so.
- **Personal Protective Equipment (PPE):** Equipment worn or used to minimize exposure to hazards.
- **Production:** The collective cast and crew, equipment, and operations assembled for the creation of a motion picture, television program, or other audiovisual content.

**Safety Philosophy**

Northbridge Films LLC believes that safety is not a separate activity but an integral part of how work is done. Every production meeting begins with a safety briefing. Every call sheet includes a safety note. Every department head is accountable for the safety of their team. This philosophy depends on open communication: crew members are encouraged to raise concerns early, and no one will be penalized for reporting a hazard or a close call.

documents.content:
**2.0 General Safety Procedures**

The procedures in this section apply to all Northbridge Films LLC productions, regardless of size or location. They are intended to establish a baseline of safe practice that every department must meet. Where a department, location, or specific task requires a higher standard, the higher standard applies.

**2.1 Pre-Production Safety Planning**

Safety planning begins before the first day of shooting. The following items must be completed during pre-production:

- The Line Producer or Production Manager appoints a Designated Safety Representative (DSR) for the production. The DSR’s name and contact information must appear on all call sheets and on the production safety board.
- A location survey is conducted for every new location, including stages, exterior locations, and rented facilities. The survey identifies potential hazards, evacuation routes, parking and staging areas, and the location of the nearest emergency medical facility.
- The production safety plan is reviewed with department heads at the first production meeting. Department heads are responsible for bringing forward any task or material they believe requires additional planning.
- Any stunt, special effect, weapon, or hazardous material is reviewed by the DSR before the work is scheduled.
- A list of emergency contacts is posted at the base camp, on the camera cart, and in the production office. The list includes local emergency services, the nearest hospital, the production’s preferred urgent care clinic, and the DSR.

**2.2 Daily Safety Briefing**

A safety briefing is held at the start of each shooting day, before any work begins. The briefing is led by the DSR or, in their absence, by the First Assistant Director. The briefing covers:

- The day’s schedule and any changes from the previous day.
- Known hazards on the current set or location, including weather conditions.
- The location of first aid kits, fire extinguishers, and evacuation assembly points.
- Any planned stunts, special effects, or other high-risk activities.
- A reminder that all incidents, including near misses, must be reported immediately.

The briefing should be kept short but must not be skipped. On days when the call time is early or the schedule is tight, the briefing still takes place. If a crew member misses the briefing, the DSR or their supervisor is responsible for reviewing the safety notes with them before they begin work.

**2.3 Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)**

PPE is provided by the production at no cost to the crew member. It is the responsibility of each crew member to wear the required PPE for their task. Department heads are responsible for enforcing PPE use within their departments.

| Task or Area | Required PPE |
| --- | --- |
| General set work (grip, electric, art, props) | Closed-toe shoes with non-slip soles; work gloves when handling lumber, metal, or cable |
| Operating or working near generators | Hearing protection (earplugs or earmuffs); closed-toe shoes |
| Working at height (ladders, lifts, scaffolding) | Approved fall protection harness and lanyard when required by the task; hard hat in designated hard hat zones |
| Handling chemicals or paints | Chemical-resistant gloves; safety glasses; respirator if required by the SDS |
| Night exterior shooting | High-visibility vest; flashlight or headlamp |
| Hot work (welding, cutting, soldering) | Welding helmet or appropriate eye protection; flame-resistant gloves; fire watch assigned |

PPE must be inspected before each use. Damaged or worn equipment is removed from service and replaced. Do not modify PPE. If a crew member believes the provided PPE is not adequate for the task, they should stop work and speak to their supervisor or the DSR.

**Appendix B – Equipment Handling and Set Safety**

B.1 General Rules for Handheld Equipment

- Do not run with any equipment, including lightweight items such as flags or C-stands.
- Carry tools point-down when walking through the set. Never carry a tool in your back pocket.
- When moving a heavy case, use a two-person carry or a cart. Do not attempt to move a case that is too heavy for you alone.
- Secure all cases in vehicles and on carts. Use ratchet straps or bungees, but do not use bungees to secure loads that could shift and strike a person.
- Report any equipment that is damaged, cracked, or malfunctioning to the department head immediately. Tag the item with a red “DO NOT USE” sticker and remove it from service until it is repaired or replaced.

B.2 Ladders and Step Ladders

- Inspect the ladder before each use. Check for loose rungs, cracked rails, and missing feet.
- Place the ladder on a firm, level surface. Do not use a ladder on a rolling platform or on a stack of boxes.
- Maintain three points of contact at all times. Do not stand on the top two rungs of a step ladder.
- Do not lean a ladder against a wall unless it is a straight ladder designed for that purpose. An A-frame ladder must be fully open with the spreader bars locked.
- When working from a ladder, keep your belt buckle between the rails. Do not overreach.
- A ladder is not a work platform. If you need to work at height for more than a few minutes, use an approved lift or scaffold.

B.3 Forklifts, Pallet Jacks, and Powered Carts

Only trained and authorized crew members may operate powered material handling equipment. The DSR keeps a list of authorized operators. If you have not been trained, do not operate the equipment, even for a short move. When a forklift is in use, the operator must:

- Sound the horn at intersections and blind corners.
- Keep the forks low to the ground when traveling.
- Never carry a passenger on the forks or in the operator’s seat area.
- Ensure the load is stable and within the rated capacity of the machine.

Pallet jacks, even manual ones, can cause serious foot and ankle injuries. Watch where you place your feet. Do not ride on a pallet jack. Keep the wheels clear of cables and hoses on the floor.
